newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Deutsche Tel out of Singapore phone race.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Tel out of Singapore phone race.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG will not join the competition when Singapore opens its telecommunications market in 2000, state television said on Monday.
Quoting unidentified industry sources, state television said Deutsche Telekom was not looking to tie up with local partners to bid for a telecoms licences.
It said the company felt it already had sufficient exposure in Asia with $2 billion worth of investments.
State television gave no further details.

Singapore plans to open up its telecoms market to competition from April 2000 and has said it will licence one or two new groups to compete directly with the current monopoly, Singapore Telecommunications Ltd, from that date.
Maritime conglomerate SembCorp Ltd and Singapore MRT Ltd, which runs Singapore's mass rapid train system, formed a consortium earlier in March to enter the race for the licence.
Other foreign companies including British Telecommunications Ltd and Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp have joined up with local partners to bid for a licence.
Analysts have said a successful bid for a licence would probably involve an initial investment of US$500 million to $1 billion.
